problem_summary.summary: Count the distinct ways to place n queens on an n by n board so that no pair shares a row, column, or diagonal.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: n. Return the number of valid board arrangements.

brute_force.explanation: Place exactly one queen per row. Try each unused column in the next row and scan all earlier queen columns to reject shared diagonals. The one-per-row and one-per-column rules still leave a large search, and every safety check scans the placed prefix.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A valid board has exactly one queen in each row and column, so its row-by-row column sequence is a permutation. The scan rejects precisely placements that share a diagonal with any earlier queen; counting each complete safe sequence counts each board once.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2 * n!) upper bound — at most O(n * n!) candidate placements are tested across the search, and each safety test may scan up to n earlier queens.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the column assignment and recursion stack.

optimized.explanation: Track occupied columns and the two diagonal families in boolean arrays. For a square coordinate (row, column), the diagonal keys are row - column + n - 1 and row + column, so a candidate can be checked and marked in constant time.
optimized.correctness_idea: A queen attacks another exactly when they share a column or one of the two diagonal keys. The arrays record all previously placed queens for those three attack relations, so a candidate is accepted exactly when it is safe; undoing each mark restores the parent state.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n * n!) upper bound — at most O(n * n!) candidate columns are tested across the search and each safety check/mark is O(1); diagonal conflicts prune most partial placements.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the three occupancy arrays and recursion stack are all linear in n.

steps.event: Place a queen in row 0, column 1.
steps.condition: Column 1 and both diagonal keys are free.
steps.action: Mark column 1 and keys 2 and 1; recurse to row 1.

steps.event: Find the first solution under row 0 column 1.
steps.condition: Column 3 is free and diagonal keys 1 and 4 are free.
steps.action: Place at (1,3), then place at (2,0) and (3,2); reaching row 4 increments count.

steps.event: Backtrack and finish the row 0 column 1 subtree.
steps.condition: All candidates below column 1 have been tested.
steps.action: Undo marks while returning; continue the root loop.

steps.event: Find the mirrored solution under row 0 column 2.
steps.condition: The branch is symmetric to the column 1 branch.
steps.action: Place queens at columns [2,0,3,1] by row; increment at row 4.

edge_cases.handling: The only square is a complete placement, so the count is 1.
Every branch is eventually blocked, so the count is 0.
Each completed row-to-column assignment increments the count once; symmetric boards remain distinct arrangements.
